rationale: The hypothesis posits that non-recurrent missense variants outside the Kelch domain (e.g., in the BTB or BACK domains) confer a milder neurodevelopmental disorder with negligible epilepsy risk. However, available clinical and molecular literature provides zero evidence for pathogenic missense variants in the BTB or BACK domains causing a milder, non-epileptic neurodevelopmental phenotype. In the benchmark series and subsequent case descriptions, 100% of reported pathogenic de novo missense variants cluster strictly within the Kelch-type beta-propeller domain (including the recurrent p.Gly357Arg variant found in 11 of 14 initial patients), and patients consistently manifest epilepsy or febrile seizures alongside intellectual disability and autism spectrum traits.

evidence.text: In the index discovery cohort, all 14 patients with pathogenic de novo missense variants in KLHL20 carried substitutions clustering exclusively within the Kelch-type beta-propeller domain, with 11 harboring the recurrent p.Gly357Arg variant; no pathogenic missense variants in the BTB or BACK domains were identified.

source.title: De novo missense variants in the E3 ubiquitin ligase adaptor KLHL20 cause a developmental disorder with intellectual disability, epilepsy, and autism spectrum …
source.quote: We studied 14 patients with de novo missense variants in KLHL20, delineating a genetic syndrome with patients having mild to severe intellectual disability, febrile seizures or epilepsy, autism spectrum disorder, hyperactivity, and subtle dysmorphic facial features. We observed a recurrent de novo missense variant in 11 patients (NM_014458.4:c.1069G>A p.[Gly357Arg]). The recurrent missense and the 3 other missense variants all clustered in the Kelch-type β-propeller domain of the KLHL20 protein, which shapes the substrate binding surface.

numbers.metric: pathogenic variants confirmed in BTB or BACK domains

evidence.text: Additional clinical descriptions of KLHL20-related disorder document severe epileptic encephalopathies such as early-onset West syndrome, reinforcing that pathogenic KLHL20 missense variants consistently drive early seizure phenotypes rather than seizure-free neurodevelopmental disorders.

source.title: Early-onset West syndrome with developmental delay associated with a novel KLHL20 variant
source.quote: with missense KLHL20 variants, six had developmental delay with epileptic encephalopathy

numbers.metric: patients with developmental delay and epileptic encephalopathy

conflicts: No verified patients harboring pathogenic de novo missense variants in the BTB or BACK domains of KLHL20 exist in published cohorts to substantiate the claim of a milder, seizure-free phenotype.

new_directions.question_text: Do rare non-synonymous variants in the BTB and BACK domains of KLHL20 in broad exome/genome sequencing repositories (e.g., gnomAD, GeneDx cohorts) demonstrate benign tolerance or an association with isolated autism/ID?
new_directions.rationale: Systematic interrogation of large clinical sequencing databases is required to determine whether BTB/BACK missense variants are non-pathogenic background variation or cause an uncharacterized milder disorder.

new_directions.question_text: How do engineered mutations in the BTB dimerization domain versus Kelch propeller substrate-binding blades affect CRL3 complex stability and substrate ubiquitination in neuronal models?
new_directions.rationale: Comparative biochemical profiling in vitro can determine if BTB mutations destabilize the Cullin3-RING ligase complex or retain residual activity relative to dominant-negative Kelch-domain alleles.
